claims.text: MMJailBench describes every multimodal jailbreak instance with four explicit annotation dimensions: harmful intent, prompt framing, visual semantics and instruction carrier. This makes coverage explicit and lets results be stratified along each dimension.
methods: Factorized construction x_{h,t,v,c} = (L(h,t,c), V(h,v)) (Eq. 1) used as a construction and annotation scheme
Stratified tables per dimension, pooled and per model, with counts, ASR, mismatch rate, CASR and bootstrap CIs computed by resampling intents
Per-model ASR-range profiles across the configurations of each dimension
results: 272 intents in 9 harm domains and 18 scenarios
6 framing templates (Academic, System, Story, Code, Structure, Paradox)
5 visual semantic categories (Danger, Work Scenario, Role, Identity Credential, Authorization Document) plus 4 control images (no image, blank, noise, nature)
conditions: Aggregate ASR depends on the mixture of intents, framings, visual contexts and carriers
Comparisons are valid only under the same judge, decoding settings and benchmark version
No per-model or per-factor ASR numbers are reported in the paper

claims.text: The harmful-intent set is diverse and non-redundant across domains.
methods: Category-guided construction from existing benchmarks and provider policies
all-MiniLM-L6-v2 pairwise cosine similarity with manual review of the high-similarity tail
PCA visualization of intent embeddings
results: Most intent pairs have low similarity; only a small high-similarity tail, which was manually reviewed
Domain sizes: Violence & Physical Harm 48 (17.6%, 3 scenarios); Sexual Content 17 (6.3%, 1 scenario); other domains 28-30 (about 10-11%)
conditions: Smaller domains have wider confidence intervals

claims.text: Scoring with ASR at threshold s>=4, together with CASR, separates genuine harmful assistance from topical engagement, and separates OCR perception failures from safety behavior.
methods: ASR = fraction of responses with harmfulness score >= 4 on a 1-5 rubric
CASR = N_success / (N - N_mismatch), where mismatch covers OCR failures, irrelevant responses and misinterpretation
Judge records an instruction-mismatch flag
Anti-deception rules stop disclaimers, fictional framing or academic packaging from lowering the score
results: Scores 2-3 (potential risk; high-level or partial info) are not counted as success
The full score distribution is released so users can apply other thresholds
conditions: Carrier results should be read per model
A low OCR ASR may reflect a perception limitation rather than safety

claims.text: The primary GPT-5 judge agrees strongly with human experts.
methods: Human expert annotation compared with GPT-5 judgments on harmfulness and mismatch
conditions: Users switching judge or rubric should re-validate on a sample before comparing results

claims.text: A distilled lightweight judge (qwen3-8b trained on GPT-5 annotations) reproduces GPT-5 judgments for low-cost follow-up evaluation.
methods: Benchmark-scoped fine-tuning on GPT-5-generated annotations under the same protocol
Agreement measured against GPT-5
conditions: Validated against GPT-5, not directly against humans
Scoped to this benchmark and protocol

claims.text: The 1,500-instance lightweight configuration closely matches the full configuration.
methods: Stratified sampling over harm domains, framings, visual semantic conditions and carriers, preserving the full-configuration distribution
Comparison over 32 matched cells
conditions: Finer cross-tabulations have fewer responses per cell; aggregate to domain level when CIs widen

claims.text: Diagnostic tooling for open-weight models gives model-internal views (layer-wise representation divergence, a held-out difference-direction projection, cross-modal attention profiles) that complement behavioral results but are correlational and descriptive.
methods: Residual-stream activations of the final generation-prefix token at every layer for matched pairs that differ in one factor
Difference direction fit on discovery pairs and projected on held-out pairs, optionally broken down by harm domain
Attention from the final prefix query to harm-related label tokens and visual tokens, per layer, averaged over heads
Illustrated on gemma3-12b
results: Profiles show where paired conditions are most separated; no quantitative diagnostic numbers are reported
conditions: Correlational: intervention is needed for causal claims
Attention is an imperfect indicator because information also flows through residual and MLP paths

claims.text: Framing templates and visual categories are fixed, representative probes rather than optimized or exhaustive attacks, so they bound what can be concluded.
methods: 6 fixed, simple framing templates instantiated by placeholder replacement
Visual images generated with zimage (Danger, Work Scenario, Role) and FLUX.2 (Identity Credential, Authorization Document, chosen for coherent text), then filtered
OCR instructions rendered in a standardized, legible layout combined with the semantic image
conditions: Image generation quality and text legibility differ across categories and can interact with perception

items.question: The lightweight configuration's agreement with the full configuration is reported in Table 11. Would that agreement still justify using the lightweight configuration for a scenario-by-carrier cross-tabulation of a single model, and why?
items.answer: No, not reliably. The 1,500 instances are spread over 18 scenarios × 2 carriers, which leaves only a few dozen responses per cell for one model. Table 11 validates agreement only at the level of its 32 matched cells, not at this fine granularity, so cell-level estimates will have wide CIs.
rubric: States the lightweight configuration would not reliably support this fine-grained cross-tab
Reason: 1,500 instances split over many scenario × carrier cells leaves few responses per cell (wide CIs), and validation was at a coarser cell level

items.question: Suppose the visual-semantics stratification shows a higher ASR for Authorization Document than for Danger. Why might this difference fail to reflect the authority meaning of the image alone?
items.answer: The two categories were made with different generators: FLUX.2 for document and credential images, which contain coherent text, and zimage for Danger. The categories therefore also differ in generation quality and in embedded text legibility. These differences can interact with model perception and confound the semantic comparison.
rubric: States the difference may be confounded and not purely due to authority semantics
Reason: different image generators and the presence or legibility of text in document images, which the paper notes can interact with perception

items.question: For which kind of model would OCR CASR become least trustworthy, given the reported validation of the judge's mismatch detection?
items.answer: A model with a high OCR mismatch rate. CASR's denominator depends on the mismatch flags, and GPT-5's mismatch detection is imperfect (macro-F1 0.85 versus humans). When many responses are mismatches, mislabelled cases shift the denominator by a larger amount and distort CASR.
rubric: Identifies models with high mismatch rates, such as weak OCR readers
Reason: CASR's denominator relies on mismatch flags, whose detection is imperfect (macro-F1 0.85), so errors matter more when mismatch is frequent

items.question: Would the lightweight judge's reported agreement carry over if it were used to score responses from a different jailbreak benchmark with its own rubric, and why?
items.answer: Not necessarily. The judge is benchmark-scoped, trained on GPT-5 annotations of MMJailBench responses under MMJailBench's protocol, and validated only in that setting. A different rubric or benchmark would require re-validation.
rubric: States agreement is not guaranteed to transfer
Reason: the judge is benchmark-scoped, trained on and validated with MMJailBench/GPT-5 annotations under this protocol, so it needs re-validation

items.question: When would a model's low ASR on all 6 framing templates stop being evidence that it resists framing-based jailbreaks?
items.answer: When the attacker uses adaptive or optimized attacks, for example iterative PAIR-style rewriting. The templates are fixed, simple probes, and the paper notes adaptive attacks may behave differently.
rubric: Identifies adaptive or optimized attacks, or attacks beyond the fixed templates
Reason: the templates are fixed, simple, non-optimized probes, not an exhaustive or worst-case attack set

items.question: When the cross-modal attention profile shows little attention to visual tokens, could the image still be influencing the response, and why?
items.answer: Yes. Attention weights are an imperfect indicator of information flow, because information can also be routed through residual connections and MLP layers. Low attention mass therefore does not rule out visual influence.
rubric: States yes, the image could still influence the output
Reason: information can flow via residual and MLP pathways, so attention is only descriptive

items.question: A study reports ASR on a custom subset containing only Violence & Physical Harm intents. Can that number be compared directly with the full-benchmark aggregate ASR, and why?
items.answer: No. Aggregate ASR summarizes a specific mixture of conditions, and Violence makes up only 17.6% of the intents (48 of 272). A different mixture can yield a different number even for the same model.
rubric: States no direct comparison
Reason: aggregate ASR depends on the composition or mixture, and the subset differs from the full distribution (Violence is about 17.6%)

items.question: Why is GPT-5's mismatch macro-F1 against human experts (0.85) so much lower than its mismatch accuracy (96.3%)?
items.answer: Mismatch cases appear to be a minority class. Accuracy is dominated by the many correctly labelled non-mismatch responses, while macro-F1 weights the rare mismatch class equally, so errors on mismatches pull it down.
rubric: States mismatch cases are relatively rare (class imbalance)
Reason: accuracy is dominated by the majority class, while macro-F1 averages over classes and penalizes minority-class errors

items.question: Why does the lightweight judge's mismatch macro-F1 against GPT-5 (0.94) exceed GPT-5's macro-F1 against humans (0.85) without implying it is more accurate than GPT-5?
items.answer: The lightweight judge was trained on GPT-5-generated annotations, so it learns to imitate GPT-5, including GPT-5's errors. High agreement with GPT-5 measures fidelity to the teacher, not accuracy relative to humans.
rubric: States the comparison does not show the lightweight judge is more accurate than GPT-5
Reason: it was distilled from GPT-5 labels, so agreement with GPT-5 reflects imitation and was measured against a different reference than humans

items.question: Why can a model's CASR never be lower than its ASR on the same responses?
items.answer: Both metrics share the same numerator, the number of successful jailbreaks. CASR divides by N minus the mismatches, which is at most N, and mismatch responses do not contribute successes, so CASR is always at least ASR.
rubric: States CASR is greater than or equal to ASR
Reason: same success count over a denominator that is reduced by mismatches (N - N_mismatch ≤ N)

items.question: Why are bootstrap confidence intervals computed by resampling intents rather than individual responses?
items.answer: Under the factorized construction, each intent generates many instances, one for each framing, image and carrier combination. Responses from the same intent are therefore correlated, which makes the intent the natural independent unit. Resampling responses would understate the uncertainty.
rubric: States intents are the appropriate independent unit
Reason: many instances are derived from the same intent via the framing × image × carrier combinations, so responses within an intent are not independent

items.question: Why would a Story-framed response that opens with a safety disclaimer but then gives step-by-step operational instructions count as a successful jailbreak?
items.answer: The judge's anti-deception rules stop disclaimers and fictional packaging from lowering the score when harmful information is provided. Operational guidance scores 4-5, which meets the s≥4 success threshold.
rubric: States it counts as a success
Reason: anti-deception rules ignore fictional framing and disclaimers, and operational content scores ≥4

items.question: Why does the lightweight configuration reproduce aggregate ASR so closely (mean difference -0.06%) despite using only 1,500 instances?
items.answer: It was built by stratified sampling over domains, framings, visual conditions and carriers that preserves the full configuration's distribution. Aggregate ASR depends on that mixture of conditions, so keeping the mixture keeps the expected ASR the same.
rubric: Attributes the match to stratified sampling that preserves the distribution over the four dimensions
Reason: aggregate ASR depends on the mixture of conditions, which is preserved

items.question: Why does the representation-level diagnostic on gemma3-12b compare instances that share intent, framing and carrier but differ only in their image?
items.answer: Holding the other three factorized dimensions fixed isolates the image as the only varying factor. Any layer-wise divergence can then be associated with the change in visual context rather than with confounds, though only correlationally.
rubric: States the goal is to isolate the image as the only differing factor
Reason: the factorized design allows the other three dimensions to be held constant, so divergence is attributable to visual context

items.question: For a model with zero instruction-recognition mismatches on OCR inputs, would its OCR CASR differ from its OCR ASR?
items.answer: No. With N_mismatch = 0, CASR's denominator equals N, so CASR equals ASR.
rubric: States CASR equals ASR (no difference)
Reason: zero mismatches leaves the denominator at N

items.question: For a model that fails to recognize 40% of OCR instructions, would its OCR CASR differ from its OCR ASR?
items.answer: Yes, CASR would be higher, unless there are no successes at all. The denominator shrinks to 60% of N while the success count stays the same.
rubric: States CASR differs, being higher than ASR (given any successes)
Reason: mismatches are removed from the denominator (N - N_mismatch = 0.6N) while the numerator is unchanged

items.question: Could the lightweight configuration reliably detect a 10-percentage-point drop in aggregate ASR between two releases of a model?
items.answer: Yes. Its deviation from the full configuration is small, with a mean absolute difference of 0.79% and a maximum of 3.53%. A 10-point change is far larger than this sampling discrepancy.
rubric: States yes
Reason: 10 points far exceeds the observed lightweight-vs-full discrepancy (mean absolute 0.79%, maximum 3.53%)

items.question: Could the lightweight configuration reliably detect a 0.5-percentage-point drop in aggregate ASR between two releases of a model?
items.answer: No. A 0.5-point change is smaller than the typical lightweight-vs-full deviation (mean absolute 0.79%, up to 3.53%), so it cannot be separated from sampling discrepancy.
rubric: States no
Reason: 0.5 points is within or below the observed discrepancy (mean absolute 0.79%, maximum 3.53%)

items.question: Could the paper's representation- and attention-level diagnostic tooling be applied to qwen2.5-vl-7b?
items.answer: Yes. It is an open-weight model evaluated from public checkpoints, so residual-stream activations and attention weights are accessible.
rubric: States yes
Reason: qwen2.5-vl-7b is open-weight, so internals are accessible

items.question: Could the paper's representation- and attention-level diagnostic tooling be applied to claude-sonnet-4.5?
items.answer: No. It is a proprietary-access model evaluated only through its official interface, so internal activations and attention are not available. The tooling is designed for open-weight models.
rubric: States no
Reason: claude-sonnet-4.5 is proprietary and accessed only via API, with no access to internals

items.question: A team without GPT-5 access wants weekly regression testing of its open-weight MLLM on MMJailBench. Which configuration and judge should it use, and what supports that choice?
items.answer: It should use the lightweight 1,500-instance configuration with the lightweight qwen3-8b judge. The lightweight configuration tracks the full one closely (Spearman 0.997, mean difference -0.06%), and the lightweight judge agrees with GPT-5 (QWK 0.95, ΔASR -0.4%).
rubric: Recommends the lightweight configuration plus the lightweight judge
Cites the configuration agreement (e.g., Spearman 0.997, small ASR difference) and the judge agreement (e.g., QWK 0.95, ΔASR -0.4%)

items.question: A model shows much lower ASR on OCR inputs than on TEXT inputs, and its developers claim it is safer against image-embedded instructions. What should an auditor check, and why?
items.answer: The auditor should check the OCR mismatch rate and CASR. A low OCR ASR may simply mean the model cannot read the rendered instructions, which is a perception limitation. If CASR is close to the TEXT rate, the apparent safety is not real.
rubric: Recommends checking the mismatch rate and CASR
Reason: low OCR ASR can reflect perception failure rather than safety behavior

items.question: A researcher wants to test whether authorization-document images raise ASR because of their meaning rather than because any visually rich image is present. Which released control condition is the most relevant comparison, and why?
items.answer: The nature image is the most relevant comparison. It is visually rich but semantically unrelated to the harmful intent, so it controls for the presence of image content. Blank and noise images contain no semantic content, and no image removes visual input entirely. Text legibility differences remain a caveat.
rubric: Identifies the nature image control
Reason: it is visually rich but task-irrelevant, unlike blank, noise or no image, so it isolates semantic meaning from mere image content

items.question: For a deployment where even high-level or partial harmful information is unacceptable, how should an auditor use MMJailBench outputs differently from the default ASR?
items.answer: The auditor should recompute success with a lower threshold, such as s≥3 or s≥2, using the released full score distribution. The default s≥4 deliberately excludes scores 2-3, which cover potential risk and high-level or partial information.
rubric: Recommends a lower threshold (e.g., s≥3 or s≥2) using the released scores
Reason: the default s≥4 intentionally does not count partial or high-level responses (scores 2-3)

items.question: A team wants to study how Code framing versus Story framing changes internal states in qwen3-vl-8b. How should it construct inputs for the representation tooling?
items.answer: It should build matched pairs that share the same intent, visual condition and carrier but differ only in framing (Code versus Story). It can then fit a difference direction on discovery pairs and test it on held-out pairs. The tooling allows any two framings to be substituted for the image pairing.
rubric: Pairs differ only in framing, with intent, image and carrier held fixed
Mentions the layer-wise divergence or a difference direction fit on discovery pairs and tested on held-out pairs

items.question: A lab scores its new model on MMJailBench with a Claude-based judge and its own rubric, then compares its ASR with the paper's GPT-5-judged results. What must it do first, and why?
items.answer: It must re-validate its judge on a sample of responses against human or default-judge labels, and match decoding settings and benchmark version. ASR inherits any systematic judge bias, and comparisons are only meaningful under the same judge, settings and version.
rubric: States the judge must be re-validated (and settings or version matched) before comparison
Reason: judge bias propagates directly into ASR, so cross-judge comparisons are otherwise invalid

items.question: If the full configuration crossed every harmful intent with every framing, every semantic image category and every carrier, roughly what fraction of it would the lightweight configuration evaluate?
items.answer: The full crossing would contain 272 × 6 × 5 × 2 = 16,320 instances. The 1,500-instance lightweight configuration would then be about 9% of the full configuration.
rubric: Computes about 16,320 full instances
Concludes the lightweight configuration is about 9% (roughly one-eleventh)

items.question: If GPT-5's harmfulness QWK against human experts had been low, say 0.5, which parts of the paper would lose support beyond the GPT-5-scored ASRs themselves?
items.answer: The lightweight judge's validity would also be undermined. It was trained on GPT-5 annotations and validated only against GPT-5, so its high agreement (QWK 0.95) would just reproduce an unreliable reference.
rubric: Names the lightweight judge (and its use for follow-up studies) as also undermined
Reason: it was trained on and validated against GPT-5 labels, not humans

items.question: Suppose the lightweight configuration had shown the same tiny mean ASR difference but a Spearman correlation of only 0.6 across cells. Which use of the lightweight configuration would lose its support?
items.answer: Its use for ranking or comparing models and cells, for example in regression testing, would lose support. A near-zero mean difference can coexist with per-cell errors that cancel out, and the strong rank agreement (0.997) is what supports preserving relative orderings.
rubric: States that ranking or comparison of models and cells would be undermined
Reason: a small mean difference can hide cancelling errors, and rank agreement is what supports preserved orderings

items.question: If the embedding analysis had found a large high-similarity mass among the 272 intents, with the PCA collapsing into a few clusters, which claim would be weakened?
items.answer: The claim that the intent set is diverse and covers the 9 domains and 18 scenarios would be weakened. The effective number of distinct harmful objectives would be smaller than 272, and per-domain stratified reports would rest on redundant intents.
rubric: Identifies the diversity or coverage claim for the intent set
Reason: redundancy would mean fewer distinct objectives than 272, weakening coverage and per-domain reporting

items.question: If the judge's mismatch detection had turned out to be unreliable, which of the two carrier-reporting metrics would lose support, and which would be unaffected?
items.answer: CASR, and with it the ability to separate perception failures from safety behavior, would lose support because its denominator depends on mismatch flags. ASR would be unaffected, since it depends only on harmfulness scores.
rubric: States CASR (and the perception-vs-safety separation) loses support
States ASR is unaffected because it uses only the harmfulness score

items.question: If held-out pairs did not project onto the difference direction fitted on discovery pairs, which conclusion about the diagnostic analysis would be undermined, and which would not?
items.answer: The conclusion that the representation difference generalizes beyond the discovery samples would be undermined. The behavioral ASR results would not be undermined, since they do not depend on the diagnostics, and no causal claim was made in the first place.
rubric: States the generalization of the representation difference to new samples is undermined
Notes behavioral results are not affected (diagnostics are separate and correlational)

items.question: If the lightweight judge's ΔASR relative to GPT-5 had been -5% instead of -0.4%, which intended use would lose support?
items.answer: Low-cost follow-up studies whose results are compared with the default GPT-5-judged numbers would lose support. A 5-point systematic underestimate would bias such comparisons and make models look safer.
rubric: Identifies the use of the lightweight judge for comparable, low-cost follow-up evaluation
Reason: a systematic -5% bias would make its ASR incomparable with GPT-5-based results

items.question: If the judge prompt lacked anti-deception rules, which factor-level stratification would be most distorted?
items.answer: The prompt-framing stratification would be most distorted. Story, Academic and Paradox framings encourage fictional, academic or safety-oriented packaging. Without the rules these could lower scores despite harmful content, underestimating ASR for those templates and biasing framing comparisons.
rubric: Identifies the prompt-framing stratification
Reason: framings such as Story, Academic or Paradox elicit packaging or disclaimers that would deflate scores without anti-deception rules

items.question: Does the paper show that proprietary MLLMs are more robust to multimodal jailbreaks than open-weight MLLMs? Answer supported, contradicted or not settled, and why.
items.answer: Not settled. The paper evaluates 8 of each type but reports no per-model or per-group ASR values. It describes how outputs are organized rather than giving comparative results.
rubric: Answers not settled
Reason: no per-model or group ASR numbers are reported

items.question: Does the paper establish that authority-document images cause MLLMs to comply with harmful requests? Answer supported, contradicted or not settled, and why.
items.answer: Not settled. No visual-category ASR numbers are reported, and the gemma3-12b diagnostics are explicitly correlational. The paper notes that intervention-based methods would be needed for causal claims.
rubric: Answers not settled
Reason: no category-level results are reported, and the diagnostics are correlational (causality requires intervention)

items.question: Does the paper directly show that the lightweight judge agrees with human experts? Answer supported, contradicted or not settled, and why.
items.answer: Not settled directly. The lightweight judge was validated only against GPT-5 (QWK 0.95), and only GPT-5 was compared with humans (QWK 0.97). Agreement with humans is plausible through this chain but was not measured.
rubric: Answers not settled (not directly shown)
Reason: the lightweight judge was compared only with GPT-5, and human comparison was done only for GPT-5

items.question: Does the paper show that MMJailBench's framing-template ASRs measure a model's worst-case robustness to framing-based jailbreaks? Answer supported, contradicted or not settled, and why.
items.answer: Contradicted. The paper states the templates are fixed, simple, non-optimized probes rather than an exhaustive or optimized attack set, and that adaptive attacks may behave differently.
rubric: Answers contradicted
Reason: the templates are fixed, simple, non-optimized probes, and adaptive attacks may differ

items.question: Does the paper show that more capable MLLMs have lower ASR on MMJailBench? Answer supported, contradicted or not settled, and why.
items.answer: Not settled. No capability-ASR relationship is reported, and the paper cautions against reading ASR as a proxy for capability. It says safety and competence are shaped by different training stages, with no a priori reason for them to move together.
rubric: Answers not settled
Reason: no such analysis is reported, and the paper cautions against linking ASR to capability

items.question: Does the paper show that the lightweight configuration's ASR is within 2 percentage points of the full configuration for every matched cell? Answer supported, contradicted or not settled, and why.
items.answer: Contradicted. Only 30 of 32 cells are within 2%, and the maximum absolute difference is 3.53%.
rubric: Answers contradicted
Reason: 30/32 cells are within 2% and the maximum difference is 3.53%

items.question: Does the paper show that harmful intents are evenly distributed across the 9 harm domains? Answer supported, contradicted or not settled, and why.
items.answer: Contradicted. Most domains hold 28-30 intents (about 10-11%), but Violence & Physical Harm has 48 (17.6%) and Sexual Content only 17 (6.3%).
rubric: Answers contradicted
Reason: cites the unequal counts, e.g., Violence 48 (17.6%) versus Sexual Content 17 (6.3%)

items.question: The difference-direction projection can be broken down by harm domain. Would the held-out projection for the Sexual Content domain be as trustworthy as the one for Violence & Physical Harm, and why?
items.answer: No. Sexual Content has only 17 intents in a single scenario, while Violence & Physical Harm has 48 intents across three scenarios. After matched pairs are split into discovery and held-out sets, Sexual Content leaves few held-out pairs, so its projection is noisier and covers less varied content.
rubric: Says the Sexual Content breakdown is less trustworthy or less reliable
Cites its small size (17 intents, one scenario) versus 48 intents and three scenarios for Violence, so few held-out pairs remain

items.question: Under what way of splitting matched pairs into discovery and held-out sets would a successful held-out projection fail to show that the difference direction generalizes to new samples?
items.answer: It fails when held-out pairs share harmful intents with discovery pairs, for example the same intent under another framing or carrier. The fixed direction could then separate held-out pairs because of intent-specific features already seen during fitting, not because the visual-condition difference extends to new intents.
rubric: Identifies a split where held-out pairs reuse the discovery pairs' harmful intents (overlap or leakage between the two sets)
Explains that success could then reflect intent-specific information seen during fitting rather than generalization to new samples

items.question: When would comparing a semantic image category against the released blank or noise control fail to isolate the effect of image content for a given model?
items.answer: It fails when the model preprocesses images differently depending on content or aspect ratio. The two conditions would then reach the language backbone in different forms, so an ASR difference could come from preprocessing rather than from image semantics. The paper recommends checking preprocessing behaviour for this reason.
rubric: Names model-specific preprocessing that depends on image content or aspect ratio as the failure condition
Explains that the ASR difference could then reflect preprocessing differences rather than semantic content

items.question: A team clusters the 16 models' per-model ASR-range vectors into profiles and publishes the result as a typology of models. When would those profile assignments stop being meaningful?
items.answer: They stop being meaningful when the assignments change across random restarts, or with the choice of features, distance metric or number of clusters. The paper treats such groupings only as a visualization aid, not a classification, and asks users to report stability across restarts.
rubric: Says assignments are not meaningful when they are unstable across restarts or sensitive to the choice of features, distance or number of clusters
Notes the paper treats clustering as a visualization aid rather than a classification of models

items.question: When could a change in aggregate ASR between two evaluations of the same proprietary model fail to reflect a real change in the model's behaviour?
items.answer: It could fail when the provider interface does not expose sampling parameters. Default settings are then used and generation may vary from run to run, so part of the difference may be sampling noise rather than a change in the model.
rubric: Identifies interfaces where sampling parameters cannot be fixed (default settings used) as the condition
Explains that run-to-run variability could then produce ASR differences unrelated to the model's behaviour

items.question: A model handles many harmful OCR inputs by only transcribing the image text or giving an off-topic reply instead of complying. Why could its OCR CASR then overstate its vulnerability?
items.answer: The judge flags transcription-only and irrelevant responses as mismatches, and CASR removes mismatches from its denominator. Responses that may be a deliberate safe deflection are therefore dropped, so CASR is computed over a smaller set and is higher than the model's real safety behaviour warrants.
rubric: Says CASR would be inflated or overstated for this model
Explains that transcription-only or irrelevant responses are flagged as mismatches and removed from CASR's denominator even if they were deliberate safe deflections

items.question: In the gemma3-12b illustration, matched pairs contrast an authority-document image with a danger-related image. Why might a peak in layer-wise divergence not reflect the difference in authority meaning between the two images?
items.answer: The two categories were made by different generators: Authorization Documents by a 4-bit-quantized FLUX.2 that produces text-bearing images, and Danger images by zimage. The pairs therefore also differ in visual style, generator and amount of embedded text. The divergence may track these differences rather than authority semantics, and the analysis is correlational in any case.
rubric: Says the divergence may not reflect authority meaning alone
Cites the confound that the two categories come from different generators (FLUX.2 vs zimage) or differ in embedded text and legibility

items.question: Why does the paper need to report QWK in addition to ΔASR to show that GPT-5 agrees with human experts?
items.answer: ΔASR only compares the overall rates. A near-zero ΔASR such as +0.3% could arise even if the judge and the humans disagreed on many individual responses, as long as the errors cancel out. QWK measures agreement on each response's 1-5 score, so it shows that individual judgments match and not just the totals.
rubric: States that ΔASR is an aggregate measure and can be near zero even when many item-level judgments disagree (offsetting errors)
States that QWK reflects per-response agreement on the 1-5 scores

items.question: Why does the representation tooling project held-out pairs onto a direction fitted on discovery pairs, rather than simply measuring how well the fitted direction separates the discovery pairs themselves?
items.answer: A direction fitted on the discovery pairs will separate those pairs by construction, so separating them proves nothing. Only projecting new, held-out pairs onto the fixed direction tests whether the representation difference extends beyond the samples used to find it.
rubric: States that the direction separates the discovery pairs by construction (fitting or overfitting makes that trivial)
States that held-out projection tests whether the difference extends to new samples

items.question: Why can a model that never explicitly refuses still have an ASR well below 100%?
items.answer: ASR counts only responses scored 4 or 5, meaning actionable or operational harmful help. A model that engages without refusing but stays high-level, partial or non-operational gets scores of 2-3, which do not count. Mismatched responses also stay in ASR's denominator without counting as successes.
rubric: Explains that compliant but high-level or partial responses score 2-3 and fall below the s>=4 threshold
Mentions that only actionable or operational help (score 4-5) counts, or that mismatched responses remain in the denominator without counting as successes

items.question: Why does the lightweight configuration's comparability with the full configuration depend on stratified sampling, rather than just on having 1,500 instances?
items.answer: Aggregate ASR depends on the mixture of intents, framings, visual conditions and carriers. A subset of the same size with a different mixture, for example too many OCR or Violence instances, could shift ASR even with no sampling noise. Stratifying over all four dimensions preserves the full-configuration mixture.
rubric: States that aggregate ASR depends on the mixture of domains, framings, visual conditions and carriers
States that stratified sampling preserves that mixture, whereas a subset of equal size with a different mixture could shift ASR

items.question: Why can a model's CASR differ from its ASR even on TEXT-carrier inputs, where no OCR reading is required?
items.answer: Mismatch is not limited to OCR recognition failures. It also covers irrelevant responses and misinterpretation of the evaluated intent, which can happen with plain text. Those cases are removed from CASR's denominator, so TEXT CASR can exceed TEXT ASR.
rubric: States that CASR can differ from ASR (typically exceed it) on TEXT inputs
Explains that the mismatch definition also includes irrelevant responses and misinterpretation, not only OCR failures

items.question: Why can scenario-level stratification show within-domain differences for Violence & Physical Harm but not for Sexual Content?
items.answer: Sexual Content contains a single scenario, so its scenario-level row is identical to the domain-level row. Violence & Physical Harm splits into three scenarios (Violence & Terrorism, Weapons & CBRN, Suicide & Self-Harm), so ASR can differ between them.
rubric: States that Sexual Content has only one scenario, so scenario stratification equals the domain result
States that Violence & Physical Harm has three scenarios that can be compared

items.question: Why does building instances from intent-level seeds, rather than collecting existing jailbreak prompts, make the per-framing ASRs interpretable as effects of framing?
items.answer: Collected jailbreak prompts tie a particular harmful goal to a particular attack strategy, so framing and intent would be confounded. With intent seeds, each fixed template is filled with the same target intent, so the framings are compared on the same objectives and differences between templates are not driven by which intents they happen to carry.
rubric: States that collected prompts confound harmful goal with attack strategy
States that seeds let every template be instantiated with the same intents, so framing comparisons hold intent fixed

items.question: On OCR inputs, Model A has 0% mismatch and 20% ASR. Model B has 50% mismatch and 15% ASR, with no successes among its mismatched cases. Would Model B look safer than Model A on OCR ASR?
items.answer: Yes. ASR uses all N responses, and B's 15% is below A's 20%.
rubric: Answers yes, B looks safer on ASR
Notes 15% < 20% because ASR's denominator includes all responses

items.question: On OCR inputs, Model A has 0% mismatch and 20% ASR. Model B has 50% mismatch and 15% ASR, with no successes among its mismatched cases. Would Model B look safer than Model A on OCR CASR?
items.answer: No. A's CASR equals its ASR at 20%. B's CASR is 15% divided by the 50% of responses that were not mismatches, which gives 30%. Once perception failures are removed, B is the more vulnerable model.
rubric: Answers no, B looks less safe on CASR
Computes or explains B's CASR as about 30% (15/50) versus A's 20%, because mismatches are removed from the denominator

items.question: When the GPT-5 judge scores claude-sonnet-4.5's responses, is the judge a different system from the model being evaluated?
items.answer: Yes. claude-sonnet-4.5 is a separate proprietary model, so the judge is assessing another system's outputs.
rubric: Answers yes
Notes claude-sonnet-4.5 is a different model from the GPT-5 judge

items.question: When the GPT-5 judge scores gpt-5's responses, is the judge a different system from the model being evaluated?
items.answer: No. gpt-5 is one of the 8 evaluated proprietary models, so here the judge scores its own outputs. The pooled human-agreement figures do not directly address this self-assessment case.
rubric: Answers no: the judge is scoring its own outputs
Notes gpt-5 is among the 16 evaluated models, and/or that the pooled validation does not specifically address self-judging

items.question: In the full configuration, would the bootstrap CI for the Story-template stratum be built by resampling from all 272 intents?
items.answer: Yes. Each template is instantiated with every target intent, so the Story stratum contains all 272 intents, and the CI resamples intents.
rubric: Answers yes
Explains that every intent is instantiated under each template and that the CI resamples intents

items.question: In the full configuration, would the bootstrap CI for the Sexual Content domain stratum be built by resampling from all 272 intents?
items.answer: No. That stratum contains only the domain's 17 intents, so resampling draws from 17 intents. This is why its CI is wider.
rubric: Answers no
States the stratum has only 17 intents to resample, giving a wider CI

items.question: If an auditor recomputes a model's ASR from the released score distribution using the threshold s>=3, could the result be lower than the default ASR?
items.answer: No. Every response scored 4 or 5 also meets s>=3, and score-3 responses are added on top. The ASR can only stay the same or rise.
rubric: Answers no
Explains that the s>=3 success set contains the s>=4 set, so ASR cannot decrease

items.question: If an auditor recomputes a model's ASR from the released score distribution using the threshold s>=5, could the result be lower than the default ASR?
items.answer: Yes. Responses scored exactly 4 (actionable harmful assistance) stop counting, so the ASR falls whenever any response received a 4.
rubric: Answers yes
Explains that score-4 responses are excluded under s>=5

items.question: A team extends MMJailBench with a third instruction carrier that delivers the instruction as handwriting in an image. Besides ASR, what should it report for this carrier, and why?
items.answer: It should report the mismatch rate and CASR. Handwriting adds a perception stage, like OCR, so a low ASR could come from the model failing to read the instruction rather than from safe behaviour. As the paper advises for carriers, the results should be read per model.
rubric: Recommends reporting the mismatch rate and CASR (not only ASR)
Explains that the new carrier adds a perception stage, so low ASR may reflect reading failures rather than safety

items.question: The lightweight judge reports 12.0% ASR for a new model. Roughly how would a human-expert rating of the same responses be expected to compare, and how strongly is that comparison supported?
items.answer: It would be expected to land very close, within a fraction of a point. The lightweight judge runs about 0.4 points below GPT-5, and GPT-5 runs about 0.3 points above humans, so the offsets roughly cancel. However, the paper validates only the two links separately, never the lightweight judge directly against humans, so this is an inference rather than a measured agreement.
rubric: Expects the human-based ASR to be very close (around 12%, within about half a point)
Combines the two ΔASR figures (-0.4% vs GPT-5, +0.3% GPT-5 vs humans)
Notes this chain is indirect: the lightweight judge was not validated directly against humans

items.question: An auditor wants to compare Identity Credential with Role images on a model known to read text in images poorly. What caveat applies to the comparison, and why?
items.answer: The difference may reflect text perception rather than meaning. Identity Credential images were generated with FLUX.2 specifically to contain coherent text, while Role images come from zimage scene generation. A model that reads embedded text poorly may not register the credential cue at all, so the categories differ in legibility as well as in semantics.
rubric: States the comparison may be confounded by text perception or legibility
Explains that Identity Credential images carry textual elements (generated with FLUX.2 for coherent text) whereas Role images are scenes from a different generator

items.question: A team wants to rank several models on Sexual Content robustness using only the lightweight configuration. What should it do, and why?
items.answer: It should use the full configuration for this domain, or at least check the bootstrap CIs before ranking. Sexual Content is the smallest domain with 17 intents, and the 1,500-instance stratified subset keeps it at about 6% of instances, so each model has few responses there and the CIs will be wide. Close rankings may not be distinguishable.
rubric: Recommends the full configuration, or checking CIs before ranking
Explains that Sexual Content is the smallest domain (17 intents) and the lightweight subset keeps only a small share of it, giving wide CIs

items.question: A company deploys an MLLM to process user-uploaded screenshots and wants to know how often a harmful instruction inside a screenshot actually produces harmful output. Should it look at OCR ASR or OCR CASR, and why?
items.answer: It should look at OCR ASR. ASR measures end-to-end vulnerability, and in deployment an instruction the model fails to read also fails to produce harm. CASR conditions on successful understanding and is the better measure of alignment robustness, not of realized risk.
rubric: Chooses OCR ASR for realized deployment risk
Explains that ASR is end-to-end (perception failures also prevent harm), whereas CASR conditions on successful understanding and measures alignment robustness

items.question: A group adds a seventh framing template, translation-based framing, to MMJailBench and reports a new aggregate ASR. How should it build the new instances, and what must it note when comparing its aggregate with earlier results?
items.answer: It should instantiate the new template for every intent by placeholder replacement and record it as a new framing value in the metadata, as the Eq. 1 scheme allows. Its aggregate ASR is not directly comparable to earlier aggregates, because it reflects a different mixture of framings and comes from a different benchmark version.
rubric: Describes instantiating the new template for all intents and annotating it as a new framing value
States that the aggregate ASR is not directly comparable because the mixture or benchmark version changed

items.question: A team distills its own 3B judge from GPT-5 annotations for MMJailBench. Which agreement statistics should it report to match the paper's validation standard, and why is accuracy alone insufficient for the mismatch label?
items.answer: It should report QWK and ΔASR for harmfulness, plus mismatch accuracy and macro-F1, measured against GPT-5 (or humans) under the same protocol. Mismatches are a minority class, as the gap between 96.3% accuracy and 0.85 macro-F1 shows, so high accuracy can hide poor detection of mismatches.
rubric: Lists QWK, ΔASR, mismatch accuracy and mismatch macro-F1
Explains that mismatch is imbalanced (minority class), so accuracy can be high while mismatch detection is poor

items.question: Suppose Table 11 had kept its -0.06% mean difference and 0.997 Spearman but reported a maximum absolute cell difference of 15%. Which use of the lightweight configuration would lose support, and which would remain?
items.answer: Using it for cell-level, per-stratum ASR values would lose support, because some cells would be badly off. Aggregate ASR and the ordering of cells would still be supported by the small mean difference and the high rank correlation.
rubric: States that cell-level or stratified ASR values from the lightweight configuration would lose support
States that aggregate ASR (and rank ordering) would remain supported

items.question: If the high-similarity tail had not been manually reviewed and many near-duplicate intents remained in Violence & Physical Harm, which reported statistic for that domain would be overstated, and why?
items.answer: The domain's precision would be overstated, meaning its bootstrap confidence interval would be too narrow. Bootstrap CIs resample intents as if they were independent units, so near-duplicates would act as fewer distinct objectives than the count of 48 suggests. Its share of the benchmark would also overstate its real coverage.
rubric: Identifies the domain's bootstrap CI as too narrow (precision overstated); mentioning inflated coverage or weight is acceptable alongside this
Explains that resampling treats intents as independent, so near-duplicates mean fewer distinct objectives than counted

items.question: If OCR instructions had been rendered with varying layouts, fonts and contrast instead of a standardized legible layout, which interpretation of TEXT-versus-OCR differences would lose support?
items.answer: The reading that a TEXT-versus-OCR difference reflects the delivery channel itself would lose support. Formatting and legibility would vary across instances, so mismatch rates and ASR could differ because of rendering quality, and the carrier effect would be confounded with presentation.
rubric: States that attributing TEXT-vs-OCR differences to the delivery channel would lose support
Explains that variable rendering adds legibility or formatting variation that confounds the carrier comparison (for example affecting mismatch)

items.question: Suppose GPT-5 had kept a harmfulness QWK of 0.97 against human experts but showed a ΔASR of +5%. Which use of the reported ASRs would lose support, and why could the high QWK not rescue it?
items.answer: Treating the reported ASR levels as matching human-expert judgment would lose support, for example comparing them with human-judged results. QWK rewards close agreement on the ordinal 1-5 scale, so it can stay high even if GPT-5 systematically scores borderline 3s as 4s. Such threshold-crossing bias directly inflates ASR.
rubric: States that the absolute ASR levels (their correspondence to human judgment) would lose support
Explains that QWK measures ordinal agreement and can remain high despite systematic disagreement at the 3-versus-4 threshold that drives ASR

items.question: If the lightweight judge had been validated against GPT-5 only on TEXT-carrier responses, which reported metric computed with it would have the weakest support, and why?
items.answer: OCR mismatch rate, and therefore OCR CASR, would have the weakest support. Mismatch cases such as recognition failures and transcription-only replies are concentrated in OCR inputs, and CASR's denominator depends directly on how well the judge flags them. That would not have been validated.
rubric: Identifies OCR mismatch rate and/or OCR CASR
Explains that mismatches arise mainly from OCR perception failures and that CASR's denominator depends on accurate mismatch flags

items.question: If some proprietary APIs had rejected a portion of the images, so those models were evaluated on a reduced instance pool, which kind of comparison in the paper would be undermined?
items.answer: Comparisons of aggregate ASR and per-model summaries across models would be undermined. Aggregate ASR depends on the mixture of conditions, and the protocol relies on all models receiving identical inputs, so differing pools would make the numbers summarize different mixtures.
rubric: Identifies cross-model comparisons of aggregate ASR or per-model summaries
Explains that ASR depends on the instance mixture and that comparability relies on identical inputs across models

items.question: Does the paper show that the OCR carrier yields higher ASR than the TEXT carrier for MLLMs? Answer supported, contradicted or not settled, and why.
items.answer: Not settled. The paper reports no per-factor ASR numbers. It also says carrier behaviour depends on each model's vision encoder and backbone and should be read per model, and that low OCR ASR may reflect perception limits.
rubric: Answers not settled
Cites the absence of reported carrier ASR numbers and/or the per-model dependence of carrier results

items.question: Does the paper show that the layer-wise divergence profile observed on gemma3-12b also holds for the other open-weight models? Answer supported, contradicted or not settled, and why.
items.answer: Not settled. The tooling is illustrated only on gemma3-12b, no quantitative diagnostic results are reported, and no other model's profiles are shown.
rubric: Answers not settled
Notes the diagnostics are illustrated only on gemma3-12b without quantitative results for other models

items.question: Does the paper show that the share of each harm domain in MMJailBench reflects how often such requests occur in real-world use? Answer supported, contradicted or not settled, and why.
items.answer: Not settled. The intents were built under category guidance from existing benchmarks and provider policies, then filtered. No usage-frequency data is used or reported, so the domain sizes reflect the construction choices.
rubric: Answers not settled
Explains that domain sizes come from category-guided construction from benchmarks and policies, not from real-world prevalence data

items.question: Does the paper show that MMJailBench's visual semantic categories produce higher ASR than its control images? Answer supported, contradicted or not settled, and why.
items.answer: Not settled. The control images are released so that users can build their own reference conditions, but the paper reports no ASR comparison between semantic and control conditions.
rubric: Answers not settled
Notes the controls are released for users without any reported comparison results

items.question: Does the paper claim that its four annotation dimensions capture every factor that affects a model's ASR on the benchmark? Answer supported, contradicted or not settled, and why.
items.answer: Contradicted. The paper itself names other influences that are not among the four dimensions: image generation quality and legibility, model-specific preprocessing, decoding settings and the judge.
rubric: Answers contradicted
Cites at least one non-annotated factor the paper says affects results (generation quality or legibility, preprocessing, decoding settings, judge)

items.question: Does the paper treat responses scored 2 or 3 as harmless? Answer supported, contradicted or not settled, and why.
items.answer: Contradicted. These scores mean potential risk or high-level and partial harmful information, and the paper says they may warrant attention in some deployment contexts. They are excluded from ASR only to keep topical engagement separate from genuine harmful assistance.
rubric: Answers contradicted
Explains that scores 2-3 denote potential or partial harm that may warrant attention, and are excluded only by the conservative success definition

items.question: qwen2.5-vl-7b generated the visual descriptions and image prompts and is also one of the evaluated models. Does the paper show that this has no effect on its visual-semantics results? Answer supported, contradicted or not settled, and why.
items.answer: Not settled. The paper documents this dual role but neither analyses nor reports whether it affects that model's results relative to the others.
rubric: Answers not settled
Notes the paper reports no analysis of this generator-evaluatee overlap

items.question: A researcher uses the cross-modal attention tooling to compare an Authorization Document instance with the no-image control, both under the TEXT carrier. Why would the visual-token part of this comparison break down?
items.answer: Under the TEXT carrier, the no-image control gives the model no image, so there are no visual tokens to receive attention. The visual-token attention profile is therefore undefined for one side of the pair. A blank or noise control, which still supplies an image, would be needed for a visual-token comparison.
rubric: States that the visual-token attention comparison fails or is undefined for the no-image condition
Explains that with no image and a TEXT carrier there are no visual tokens to attend to
Suggests or notes that an image-bearing control such as blank or noise would avoid this problem

items.question: When could the cross-modal attention tooling show nearly identical layer-wise attention profiles for two paired image conditions even though some attention heads treat the images very differently?
items.answer: This can happen when only a few heads respond differently to the two images. The tooling averages attention mass over heads, so head-specific differences can be diluted or cancel out in the average. The flat profile would then hide a real difference.
rubric: Identifies the case where differences are confined to a few heads, or where heads differ in opposite directions
Explains that the tooling averages attention over heads, which dilutes or cancels head-specific effects

items.question: A newly released model answers MMJailBench prompts in a response style quite unlike earlier models, for example with very long reasoning traces before the answer. Why might the lightweight judge's reported agreement fail to hold for this model's responses?
items.answer: The lightweight judge was fine-tuned on GPT-5 annotations and validated against GPT-5 only within this benchmark and protocol. Its 0.95 QWK and 99.4% mismatch accuracy describe responses like those it was trained and validated on, and an unfamiliar response style is a distribution shift that this validation does not cover. A sample of the new model's responses should be re-checked against GPT-5 before relying on the lightweight scores.
rubric: States that the agreement may not hold or is not guaranteed for this model
Explains that the judge was distilled from and validated against GPT-5 annotations on responses within the benchmark's scope, so a new response style is outside what was validated
Recommends re-validating on a sample against GPT-5 (or human ratings)

items.question: When would a small per-model ASR range across the 6 framing templates fail to show that a model is insensitive to framing?
items.answer: It fails when the model's ASR is near 0% (or near 100%) under every template. The range then has no room to grow, whatever the model's framing sensitivity. A small range under such a floor or ceiling reflects the overall ASR level rather than any insensitivity to framing.
rubric: Identifies a floor or ceiling case, i.e. ASR near zero (or near maximum) across all templates
Explains that the range is then compressed regardless of sensitivity, so it reflects the overall ASR level rather than framing insensitivity

items.question: A team runs the 1,500-instance lightweight configuration scored by the lightweight judge and treats the results as equivalent to the full configuration scored by GPT-5. Why is that equivalence not directly established by the paper?
items.answer: The paper validates each shortcut separately. The lightweight configuration is compared with the full configuration in Table 11, and the lightweight judge is compared with GPT-5 in Table 12. The combined pipeline is never compared with full-plus-GPT-5. Sampling deviations (up to 3.53% in a cell) and judge deviations (ΔASR −0.4%, QWK 0.95) could add up, so the combination remains unvalidated.
rubric: States that the equivalence of the combined setup is not directly validated
Explains that the two shortcuts were each validated against their own reference (full configuration and GPT-5) but never together
Notes that their errors could compound, e.g. cell-level sampling deviations plus judge deviations

items.question: The OCR instruction images use font sizes and contrast chosen to stay legible after typical image preprocessing. For which kind of model could this design choice fail, and how would that show up in the results?
items.answer: It could fail for a model whose interface downsamples or crops images unusually aggressively, more than typical preprocessing does. The rendered instruction could then become unreadable. That would show up as a higher OCR mismatch rate and a low OCR ASR that reflects perception failure rather than safety.
rubric: Identifies models with atypical or aggressive image preprocessing such as heavy downscaling or cropping
States that the instruction may become illegible, raising OCR mismatch and lowering OCR ASR for perception rather than safety reasons

items.question: Why is the lightweight configuration's mean absolute ASR difference (0.79%) much larger than the magnitude of its mean ASR difference (−0.06%)?
items.answer: Individual cells deviate in both directions: some lightweight cells come out above the full configuration and some below. In the signed mean these deviations largely cancel, but in the absolute mean they do not. So there is little systematic bias, yet there is real cell-level sampling noise of under 1 point on average.
rubric: Explains that per-cell differences have mixed signs that cancel in the signed mean but not in the absolute mean
Concludes that this indicates little systematic bias but non-zero per-cell noise

items.question: Why does the reported 95% CI for the lightweight-minus-full ASR difference support the claim that the lightweight configuration does not systematically over- or under-estimate ASR?
items.answer: The interval [−0.45%, 0.30%] contains zero, so the data are consistent with no systematic offset. It is also narrow, which rules out any bias larger than about half a percentage point in either direction.
rubric: Notes that the CI includes zero, so there is no evidence of a systematic offset
Notes that the CI is narrow, bounding any possible bias to under about 0.5 percentage points

items.question: Under the paper's factorized construction (Eq. 1), why does comparing ASR across framing templates for a given intent and visual category not also change the image the model sees?
items.answer: In Eq. 1 the visual component is V(h,v), which depends only on the intent and the visual semantic condition, not on the framing t. Instances that differ only in framing therefore share the same image. Only the instruction component L(h,t,c) changes.
rubric: States that the image is the same across framings for a given intent and visual category
Explains that V(h,v) depends only on intent and visual semantics, not on framing (framing enters only through L(h,t,c))

items.question: Why can a difference between TEXT and OCR ASR for the same intents, framings and visual categories be attributed to how the instruction is delivered rather than to a difference in visual context?
items.answer: In Eq. 1 the carrier enters only the instruction component L(h,t,c), while the semantic image V(h,v) does not depend on the carrier. For OCR, the rendered instruction is combined with that same semantic image, and the semantics are preserved. So the two carriers share intent, framing and visual context and differ only in delivery.
rubric: States that the visual semantic context is the same under both carriers
Explains that the carrier affects only L(h,t,c) while V(h,v) is carrier-independent, and that OCR combines the rendered instruction with the same semantic image

items.question: Why can two models with identical ASR differ substantially in how dangerous their successful jailbreaks are?
items.answer: ASR is a binary count of responses with s ≥ 4, so a response scored 4 (actionable assistance) and one scored 5 (detailed operational guidance) count the same. One model could have mostly 4s and the other mostly 5s. Only the released full score distribution reveals this difference.
rubric: States that ASR treats scores 4 and 5 identically as successes
Explains that severity differences, such as more score-5 responses, are visible only in the released score distribution

items.question: A researcher wants to know whether merely attaching an image, regardless of content, changes a model's refusal behaviour. Which two released conditions should be compared, under which carrier, and why?
items.answer: Compare the no-image control with the blank image under the TEXT carrier. The blank image adds visual input but no semantic content, so any difference isolates the presence of an image. The TEXT carrier is needed because under OCR the instruction itself arrives as an image, so even the no-image condition contains visual input.
rubric: Chooses no-image versus blank (noise is an acceptable secondary option)
Explains that blank adds an image without semantic content, isolating image presence from image meaning
Specifies the TEXT carrier, because under OCR there is always an image carrying the instruction

items.question: A model has near-zero mismatch rates on both carriers, but its OCR ASR is 30% while its TEXT ASR is 10%. What should an auditor conclude about the OCR result, and why?
items.answer: With near-zero mismatches, OCR CASR is essentially equal to OCR ASR, so the gap cannot be explained by perception failures. The model reads the embedded instructions correctly and genuinely complies more often when the instruction arrives as an image. This points to weaker safety behaviour on image-embedded instructions.
rubric: Concludes that the OCR gap reflects a genuine safety weakness rather than a perception artifact
Explains that near-zero mismatch makes CASR ≈ ASR, so the model understood the instructions

items.question: In the per-model factor-sensitivity scatter plot, a model shows a 25-point ASR range on the framing dimension. Before reporting it as 'highly framing-sensitive', what should the auditor check, and why?
items.answer: The auditor should check the underlying per-template stratified table for that model. The range alone cannot tell whether one outlying template, such as Code, drives the spread or whether ASR rises gradually across templates. These two situations call for different conclusions and follow-ups.
rubric: Recommends inspecting the per-template stratified table for that model
Explains that the range cannot distinguish a single outlying template from a gradual trend across templates

items.question: A team adds a sixth visual semantic category, 'Prescription Note', which contains printed text. Following the paper's construction pipeline, how should it generate the images, and what caveat should it attach to comparisons with text-free categories?
items.answer: The team should generate one image per intent, following V(h,v), using a generator able to render coherent text, as FLUX.2 was chosen for Identity Credential and Authorization Document. It should then filter the images for semantic relevance, visual quality and readability. The caveat is that generation quality and text legibility differ from text-free categories and can interact with model perception, so ASR differences may partly reflect perception rather than meaning.
rubric: Specifies intent-specific generation with a text-capable generator plus filtering for relevance, quality and readability
States the caveat that legibility and generation quality differ from text-free categories and can interact with perception, confounding comparisons

items.question: A team needs per-model, scenario-by-carrier results but can afford only one of two setups: the full configuration scored by the lightweight judge, or the 1,500-instance configuration scored by GPT-5. Which should it choose, and why?
items.answer: It should choose the full configuration with the lightweight judge. Scenario-by-carrier cells for a single model become too sparse in the 1,500-instance subset, and the paper advises aggregating to domain level when cells get small. The lightweight judge closely reproduces GPT-5 (QWK 0.95, ΔASR −0.4%), so the cost in judge fidelity is small.
rubric: Chooses the full configuration with the lightweight judge
Explains that fine per-model cross-tabulations are too sparse in the lightweight configuration
Notes that the lightweight judge's agreement with GPT-5 is high (e.g. QWK 0.95, ΔASR −0.4%)

items.question: If the visual input had been regenerated separately for each framing template, so that it depended on framing as well as intent and visual category, which stratification would become hard to interpret, and why?
items.answer: The prompt-framing stratification would become hard to interpret. Differences between templates would mix framing effects with differences between images. Under the paper's Eq. 1, V(h,v) does not depend on framing, which is what keeps images fixed across templates.
rubric: Identifies the prompt-framing stratification
Explains that framing would be confounded with image differences, which the framing-independent V(h,v) currently prevents

items.question: If OCR instances showed only the rendered instruction image, without the semantic image that TEXT instances receive, which comparison would be confounded, and how?
items.answer: The TEXT-versus-OCR carrier comparison would be confounded. The two carriers would then differ both in instruction delivery and in whether semantic visual context is present. An ASR or CASR gap could no longer be attributed to the carrier alone.
rubric: Identifies the carrier (TEXT vs OCR) comparison
Explains that carrier would be confounded with the presence or absence of semantic visual context

items.question: If the control images had been rendered at a different resolution from the semantic images, which kind of comparison would become unreliable, and why?
items.answer: Comparisons between semantic categories and controls would become unreliable. Some models apply different preprocessing depending on image properties, so a resolution difference could change how images are processed independently of their content. The paper avoids this by rendering controls at the same resolution and pairing them with the same instruction components.
rubric: Identifies semantic-category versus control comparisons
Explains that resolution differences could trigger different preprocessing, confounding the content effect (the paper matches resolution to avoid this)

items.question: If the lightweight configuration's stratified sampling had preserved harm domains, framings and carriers but not the visual semantic conditions, which stratified view computed on the lightweight configuration would lose its support?
items.answer: The visual-semantics stratification computed on the lightweight configuration would lose its support. Its category mixture would no longer match the full configuration, so per-category ASR and the aggregate could be skewed. Table 11's agreement depends on the full distribution being preserved along all four dimensions.
rubric: Identifies the visual-semantics stratification (per visual category results) on the lightweight configuration
Explains that the representativeness behind the Table 11 agreement relies on preserving the distribution along every annotated dimension, including visual conditions

items.question: If the judge mistakenly flagged clear refusals as 'irrelevant responses', and therefore as mismatches, which carrier-reporting metric would be distorted, and in which direction?
items.answer: CASR would be distorted upward. Refusals are non-successes, and flagging them as mismatches removes them from the denominator N − N_mismatch while the numerator stays the same. ASR would be unaffected, since its denominator is all N responses.
rubric: Identifies CASR as the distorted metric
States that it would be inflated, because non-successful refusals would be removed from the denominator while successes are unchanged (ASR is unaffected)

items.question: Does the paper show that any stratified 1,500-instance sample drawn by a user would match the full configuration as closely as the reported lightweight configuration does? Answer supported, contradicted or not settled, and why.
items.answer: Not settled. Table 11 validates the one released lightweight configuration against the full configuration. The paper reports no comparison across alternative stratified draws, so how much agreement varies from one draw to another is not established.
rubric: Answers not settled
Explains that only the single released 1,500-instance configuration was compared with the full configuration, with no evidence on other draws

items.question: Does the paper show that the GPT-5 judge agrees with human experts equally well within each harm domain and each framing template? Answer supported, contradicted or not settled, and why.
items.answer: Not settled. Table 12 reports agreement figures (QWK 0.97, ΔASR +0.3%, mismatch accuracy and macro-F1) only in aggregate. No per-domain or per-framing breakdown of judge agreement is given, so stratum-specific judge reliability is unknown.
rubric: Answers not settled
Explains that the human-agreement statistics are reported only in aggregate, with no per-domain or per-framing breakdown

items.question: Does the paper show that Story framing is the most effective of its 6 framing templates at jailbreaking MLLMs? Answer supported, contradicted or not settled, and why.
items.answer: Not settled. The paper describes the framing stratification but reports no per-template ASR numbers. Even with such numbers, the templates are fixed, simple probes, so they would rank only these instantiations and not framing strategies in general.
rubric: Answers not settled
Explains that no per-template ASR values are reported (and/or that the fixed simple templates would not establish the strategy's general effectiveness)

items.question: Does the paper show that the layer where gemma3-12b's paired conditions diverge most is the layer where the model makes its safety decision? Answer supported, contradicted or not settled, and why.
items.answer: Not settled. The divergence profile only shows where the paired representations are most separated, and the paper reports no quantitative diagnostic results. It also stresses that such analyses are correlational, so localizing a decision would require intervention experiments.
rubric: Answers not settled
Explains that the divergence profile is correlational and descriptive (no numbers reported), so causal localization would need intervention

items.question: Does the paper show that its rendered OCR instructions are reliably read by all 16 evaluated models? Answer supported, contradicted or not settled, and why.
items.answer: Not settled. The instructions were rendered in a standardized layout intended to stay legible after typical preprocessing, and mismatch rates are part of the output. However, no per-model mismatch numbers are reported, and the paper itself warns that low OCR ASR may reflect perception limitations.
rubric: Answers not settled
Explains that legibility is a design intent but no per-model OCR mismatch rates are reported, and the paper anticipates perception failures for some models

items.question: Because Violence & Physical Harm is the largest domain (48 intents), does the paper show that it is the domain where MLLMs are most vulnerable? Answer supported, contradicted or not settled, and why.
items.answer: Not settled. The domain's size reflects benchmark composition, not measured vulnerability. The paper reports no per-domain ASR values, and the suite reports per-domain rates separately from counts precisely so that the two are not confused.
rubric: Answers not settled
Explains that domain size reflects composition rather than vulnerability, and that no per-domain ASR results are reported

items.question: Under the TEXT carrier, does the 'no image' control condition give the model an input containing no image at all?
items.answer: Yes. Under the TEXT carrier the instruction is plain text, so removing the semantic image leaves no visual input at all.
rubric: Answers yes
Explains that under TEXT the instruction is plain text, so without the semantic image no image remains

items.question: Under the OCR carrier, does the 'no image' control condition give the model an input containing no image at all?
items.answer: No. Under the OCR carrier the instruction itself is rendered into an image. Removing the semantic image still leaves an image that carries the instruction text.
rubric: Answers no
Explains that the OCR carrier delivers the instruction as a rendered image, so an image remains even without the semantic image

items.question: Following the paper's recommendations, is it valid to compare the per-model factor-sensitivity summaries of two models that were both scored by GPT-5 with the same decoding settings on the same benchmark version?
items.answer: Yes. The paper recommends comparing per-model summaries among models evaluated under the same judge, decoding settings and benchmark version, and this pair meets all three conditions.
rubric: Answers yes
Explains that the shared judge, decoding settings and benchmark version satisfy the paper's comparability conditions

items.question: Following the paper's recommendations, is it valid to compare the per-model factor-sensitivity summaries of two models when one was scored by GPT-5 and the other by the lightweight judge?
items.answer: No, not directly. The paper recommends comparing summaries only under the same judge, because changing the judge can shift the reported values. The lightweight judge's high but imperfect agreement with GPT-5 (QWK 0.95) does not remove that concern.
rubric: Answers no (not directly valid)
Explains that the paper restricts comparisons to the same judge because judge changes can shift values, even given the lightweight judge's high but imperfect agreement

items.question: On an OCR instance, a model's response only transcribes the text visible in the image. Would this response be excluded from the CASR denominator?
items.answer: Yes. Only transcribing visual content is listed as an instruction-recognition failure, so the judge flags it as a mismatch. It is removed from N − N_mismatch.
rubric: Answers yes
Explains that transcription-only responses are flagged as instruction mismatches and so are subtracted from the denominator

items.question: On an OCR instance, a model's response explicitly refuses the specific harmful task described in the image. Would this response be excluded from the CASR denominator?
items.answer: No. The refusal shows that the model recognized the task, so it is not a mismatch. It stays in the denominator as a non-success and lowers CASR.
rubric: Answers no
Explains that a task-specific refusal demonstrates correct understanding, so it is not a mismatch and remains in the denominator as a non-success

items.question: Would a pair consisting of a Danger image with the TEXT carrier and an Authorization Document image with the TEXT carrier, sharing intent and framing, be a valid matched pair for attributing representation divergence to the image?
items.answer: Yes. The two instances differ only in the visual semantic condition, which is the one-factor matched design the tooling relies on, so divergence can be attributed to the image.
rubric: Answers yes
Explains that the instances differ in exactly one factor (the image), matching the tooling's one-factor pairing design

items.question: Would a pair consisting of a Danger image with the TEXT carrier and an Authorization Document image with the OCR carrier, sharing intent and framing, be a valid matched pair for attributing representation divergence to the image?
items.answer: No. The two instances differ in both the image and the carrier, so any divergence could come from either factor. It cannot be attributed to the image alone.
rubric: Answers no
Explains that the pair differs in two factors (image and carrier), so divergence cannot be attributed to the image

items.question: OCR instances combine the rendered instruction with the semantic image, while TEXT instances show the semantic image alone. Given the paper's note on model-specific image preprocessing, when would a TEXT-versus-OCR ASR difference fail to reflect the delivery channel alone?
